title: Relative module flatness is independent of arbitrary source and target etale charts
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism. Let $M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and fix $x\in|X|$ [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Consider all diagrams of $S$-schemes $U\xrightarrow{h}V$ with representable etale maps $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$ satisfying $fa=bh$, together with $u\in U$ mapping to $x$. Let $F$ be the quasi-coherent Zariski module on $U$ corresponding to $a^*M$ under [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], where pullback is [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Then $(F)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{V,h(u)}$ for some such diagram and point if and only if it is flat over that local ring for every such diagram and point. Stalks are ordinary Zariski stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], with scalar action induced by $h$; module flatness means exactness of tensoring [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No finiteness, separation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed, and the source chart need not be surjective.

proof.text: There is a compatible chart point over $x$. Indeed [def-trf-algebraic-space] provides a surjective etale scheme atlas $b_0:V_0\to Y$. The existence clause of [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts] gives $a_0:U_0\to X$ surjective etale and $h_0:U_0\to V_0$ with $fa_0=b_0h_0$. Take a field-valued representative of $x$ from [def-a1-space-point-topology]. By the scheme-test meaning of surjectivity in [def-trf-algebraic-space], its base change to $U_0$ is a nonempty scheme. Any point of that base change gives $u_0\in U_0$ over $x$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(u_0)$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; by [def-weil-geometric-point] it defines $\bar u_0:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U_0$ centered at $u_0$. Fix $\bar x=a_0\bar u_0$ and $\bar y=f\bar x$ for the remaining steps.

source.place: Tag 05VU, choice of geometric point and compatible diagrams; compatible atlas existence is spaces.tex Tag 02X1 (lemma-lift-morphism-presentations).

proof.text: Let $(U,V,a,b,h,u)$ be any diagram and point in the statement. By [lem-sfb-etale-geometric-point-specified-lift] the fixed $\bar x$ lifts to $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ centered at this specified $u$. Put $\bar v=h\bar u$, $v=h(u)$, $B=\mathcal O_{U,u}$, $R=\mathcal O_{V,v}$, and $N=F_u$. Then $b\bar v=\bar y$. The ring identifications in [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness], applied to $a$ and $b$, identify $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}=B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$. By [lem-sfb-space-quasicoherent-geometric-stalk-tensor] there is a canonical $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$-linear isomorphism $N\otimes_B B^{\mathrm{sh}}\simeq M_{\bar x}$. Its $R$-action is the restriction of the action through $R\to R^{\mathrm{sh}}\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$: the equality $fa=bh$ says a germ on $V$ pulls back to the same germ on a common pointed neighbourhood on either path. The tensor comparison sends $n\otimes c$ to the product of the two germs, so multiplication by this pulled-back germ agrees on both sides.

source.place: Tag 05VU (lemma-flat-at-point), proof for an arbitrary compatible chart diagram.

proof.text: The local ring map $B\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat]. Apply [lem-trf-flatness-faithfully-flat-extension] with $A=R$, $B=B$, $C=B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and module $N$: it gives $N$ flat over $R$ if and only if $B^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_B N$ is flat over $R$. The tensor symmetry $c\otimes n\mapsto n\otimes c$ and step 2 identify this last module with $M_{\bar x}$ as an $R$-module. Now apply [lem-sfb-strict-henselization-module-flatness] to the $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-module $M_{\bar x}$. We obtain $F_u$ flat over $\mathcal O_{V,h(u)}$ if and only if $M_{\bar x}$ is flat over $R^{\mathrm{sh}}=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$. This criterion uses only the fixed $\bar x$ and its image $\bar y$. In particular it is independent of the diagram and $u$. Neither $R\to B$ nor $f$ is assumed flat.

source.place: Tag 05VU, final paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 0584 (lemma-flatness-descends-more-general), (2); more-algebra.tex Tag 07QM (lemma-dumb-properties-henselization), (1); flat.tex Tag 05VL (lemma-flat-up-down-henselization), (1) iff (3).

proof.text: If flatness holds for some diagram and point, step 3 gives flatness of the fixed $M_{\bar x}$ over $\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$, and step 3 in reverse then gives flatness for every diagram and point. Conversely, if flatness holds for every diagram and point, apply it to the witness of step 1 to obtain the existential condition. A source chart missing $x$ contributes no points to the universal condition. If $X$ is empty there is no $x$ under consideration.

lean.statement: theorem module_flat_some_iff_every_chart {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (M : X.QCoh) (x : Point X.obj.obj) : (∃ (U : X.EtaleSite) (V : Y.EtaleSite) (h : U.obj.left ⟶ V.obj.left) (u : X.etaleForget.obj U), U.obj.hom ≫ f.hom.hom = yoneda.map h ≫ V.obj.hom ∧ schemePointMap U.obj.hom u = x ∧ Module.Flat (V.obj.left.left.presheaf.stalk (h.left u)) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (h.left.stalkMap u).hom).obj ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor (X.etaleForget.obj U).toRingedSpace u).obj ((X.schemeRestriction U).obj M.obj)))) ↔ (∀ (U : X.EtaleSite) (V : Y.EtaleSite) (h : U.obj.left ⟶ V.obj.left) (u : X.etaleForget.obj U), U.obj.hom ≫ f.hom.hom = yoneda.map h ≫ V.obj.hom → schemePointMap U.obj.hom u = x → Module.Flat (V.obj.left.left.presheaf.stalk (h.left u)) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (h.left.stalkMap u).hom).obj ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor (X.etaleForget.obj U).toRingedSpace u).obj ((X.schemeRestriction U).obj M.obj))))
